senses.definition: An English unit of land area (symbol: a. or ac.) originally denoting a day's ploughing for a yoke of oxen, now standardized as 4,840 square yards or 4,046.86 square metres.

quotes.text: Buried within the Mediterranean littoral are some seventy to ninety million tons of slag from ancient smelting, about a third of it concentrated in Iberia. This ceaseless industrial fueling caused the deforestation of an estimated fifty to seventy million acres of woodlands.
quotes.reference: 2006, Edwin Black, chapter 2, in Internal Combustion:

subsenses.definition: (Chester, historical) An area of 10,240 square yards or 4 quarters.

senses.definition: Any of various similar units of area in other systems.
(informal, usually in the plural) A wide expanse.
examples: I like my new house—there’s acres of space!

senses.definition: (informal, usually in the plural) A large quantity.
(obsolete) The acre's breadth by the length, English units of length equal to the statute dimensions of the acre: 22 yd (≈20 m) by 220 yd (≈200 m).
(obsolete) A duel fought between individual Scots and Englishmen in the borderlands.
